description.texte: Superpowers imposes a real method on your coding agent. It doesn't rush into the code: it asks what you're trying to do, shows you the spec in readable chunks, then builds an implementation plan once the design is approved. Skills trigger on their own, with no command to type.
passages: Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.
it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.
Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.
After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan
because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special

interet.texte: The plan splits the work into 2- to 5-minute tasks, with files, code, and checks. TDD is strict: code written before its test is deleted. Between tasks, a review ranks issues by severity, and a critical issue blocks the next step. According to the author, the agent can thus run autonomously for a few hours without straying from the plan.
passages: Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.
Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit.
It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.
Deletes code written before tests.
Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.
It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

exemple_usage.texte: For a new feature: brainstorming pins down the request, writing-plans breaks it into small tasks, then implementation starts with a failing test, before the minimal code.
passages: Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it
